# Libraries and provenance

This is the optional monthly/weekly and forecasting profile. The submitted
report's default daily analysis is in `Code.Rmd` and `Results/Report-aligned/`.
Google Trends and financial stress are outside that submitted project scope.

This notebook follows the original repository's R Markdown format. Its modular R
source files are in `R/`; the complete original notebook, data, and MIT license
are preserved in `../Original-paper/`. All analysis below is performed by R.

The frozen project sample contains 20 fan tokens and Bitcoin, Ethereum, and
Chiliz benchmarks, with a daily cutoff of 19 September 2026. The analytical
monthly sample ends in August 2026, the last complete month. Partial final weeks
are also omitted. No live market-data request is needed to reproduce results.

```{r versions}
data.frame(package = names(package_versions), version = unname(package_versions))
```

Set `params = list(regenerate = TRUE)` in `rmarkdown::render()` to execute every
stage below. The default renders the included, validated result tables without
refitting hundreds of forecasting models. `Rscript run_paper_extensions.R` is the direct
command-line equivalent of a full regeneration.

# Raw data and processing

`R/01_process_data.R` parses all 23 archived Yahoo chart JSON responses, recovers
UTC dates, clips the sample, checks duplicates, constructs daily calendars, and
calculates returns only between adjacent valid daily prices. It flags extremes
without deleting them. Monthly and weekly inputs are arithmetic mean prices,
matching the original paper code. The first return of each modeling block is
padded with zero, as in the original notebook.

```{r process, eval=params$regenerate}
data <- process_data()
```

```{r quality}
knitr::kable(read_table("Results/data_quality.csv"))
```

# Detection phase

The actual paper packages are used: `exuber::radf()` on monthly price levels,
`exuber::radf_mc_cv()` for 1,000 finite-sample Monte Carlo draws at seed 4,
`exuber::datestamp()` for 95% episodes, and `cpm::processStream()` with the
Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic on monthly log returns. Endpoint-specific BSADF
critical values are exported. Monthly ARL0 is 500; weekly ARL0 is 5,000.
Startup is 20% of each block, with a floor of 20 observations. This adjustment
and the explicit Monte Carlo critical values are documented in Methodology.txt.

```{r detection, eval=params$regenerate}
run_detection(data)
```

```{r recursive-tests}
tests <- read_table("Results/psy_test_summary.csv")
knitr::kable(tests[tests$test == "GSADF", c("asset_id", "observations", "min_window", "statistic", "critical_95", "reject_95")], digits = 4)
```

```{r episodes}
knitr::kable(read_table("Results/psy_euphoric_episodes.csv"))
```

```{r change-points}
knitr::kable(read_table("Results/ks_cpm_change_points.csv"))
```

```{r detection-figures, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(list.files("Figures", pattern = "_detection[.]png$", full.names = TRUE))
```

KS distribution changes are statistical regimes. The paper's green-energy phase
labels are not transferred to fan tokens. BSADF euphoric episodes are distinct
from complete formation, burst, and decline cycles.

# Propagation phase

The available-data adaptation uses token, BTC, and CHZ price levels with
`urca::ca.jo(type="trace", K=2, ecdet="none", spec="longrun")`. VECMs are fitted
using `urca::cajorls()` only when the 5% sequential trace rule selects an
intermediate rank. Unit-root diagnostics are supplied. A p=1 VAR and package
Granger F-tests summarize benchmark predictability. These results concern a
different variable system from the paper's FSI/oil system and cannot support
its financial-stress conclusion.

```{r propagation, eval=params$regenerate}
run_propagation(data)
```

```{r johansen}
knitr::kable(read_table("Results/benchmark_johansen_trace.csv"), digits = 4)
```

No fan-token Google Trends data or financial-stress series was supplied. Their
status is recorded in `Results/paper_extension_status.csv`. Original green-energy search
data remain in Original-paper as reference material, not fan-token sentiment.

# Forecasting phase

The expanding-window exercise predicts one monthly observation at a time.
`forecast::auto.arima(seasonal=FALSE)` and the original BSTS state specification
are used. BSTS has 1,000 MCMC draws, seed 9, and 10% suggested burn-in. Holdout
length is at most the paper's 37 months; each series retains at least 36 training
months because the fan-token histories are shorter than the paper's sample.

The code also implements ARIMAX if an actual, complete fan-token search-interest
input is later supplied. Current results contain the two available univariate
baselines. The current-interest ARIMAX model is a conditional nowcast; it is not
a forecast available before target-month search interest is observed.

```{r forecasts, eval=params$regenerate}
run_forecasting(data)
```

```{r forecast-tables}
knitr::kable(read_table("Results/forecast_accuracy.csv"), digits = 4)
```

Metrics are reported on both log-price and USD-price scales. Exponentiated
log-point predictions are labeled median price forecasts. Diebold-Mariano tests
use `multDM::DM.test()` and squared error; per-token model confidence sets use
`MCS::MCSprocedure(alpha=0.15, B=5000, statistic="TR")`. Without search-interest
data, the comparison set contains ARIMA and BSTS. No superiority of an unavailable
ARIMAX model is asserted.

```{r forecast-figures, echo=FALSE, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics(list.files("Figures", pattern = "_forecasts[.]png$", full.names = TRUE))
```

# Simulation appendix

The paper's original eGARCH bubble-generation and 1,000-replication simulation
code is retained, unmodified, in `../Original-paper/Code-and-Data/Code.Rmd`.
Those simulations assess the original paper's methods; they are not empirical
fan-token observations and are not counted among this project's results.
